If rock unit D is an intrusion, which geologic principle would you use to determine the age of rock unit D with respect to rock unit E (the fault)? 

The principle of cross-cutting relationships would be used to determine the age of rock unit D with respect to rock unit E. This principle states that a feature that cuts across other rocks is younger than the rocks it cuts across. Since rock unit D is an intrusion, it cuts across rock unit E, indicating that rock unit D is younger than rock unit E.
